name: The Great Linden of the Muhlacker

location.address: Am Muhlacker, beside the town wall near the Rossmuhle youth hostel, Rothenburg ob der Tauber

access: Free, on a public path along the town wall near the youth hostel
transport: About 10 minutes on foot south of the Marktplatz, near the Rossmuhle youth hostel below the Spitalbastei
verify_notes: Not a candidate from the register list in the brief; found independently via baumkunde.de. A stone inscription on the adjacent town wall reads 'A. 1587 IST DIE LINDEN GESEGZET' (the linden was planted in 1587), giving a documented planting date for this specimen (2026 minus 1587 = 439 years; age band widened to 400-480 to stay honest about the last-measurement lag). Circumference recorded by baumkunde.de as about 6 metres. Baumkunde.de's own visit record (last visited 20 March 2025) describes it as 'alte fragmentierte Linde' (an old, fragmented veteran) but 'vital, treibt jaehrlich noch aus' (vital, still leafs out every year) and lists it as publicly accessible. Second, independent source: a Carl Theodor Reiffenstein pencil drawing dated 16 July 1869, held by the Staedel Museum, titled 'Grosse Linde am Muehlacker in Rothenburg ob der Tauber', depicting a linden as the primary subject at this same site beside the town wall, i.e. a large, notable linden has stood and been recorded at this exact spot for over 150 years. Species given as Sommer-Linde by baumkunde.de, which is Tilia platyphyllos (large-leaved lime); note this is sometimes confused with Tilia cordata (small-leaved lime, also called 'Sommerlinde' colloquially in some regions), so a reader correction on the exact Tilia species would be welcome. Not one of the 28 Bavarian Naturdenkmal register candidates in the brief; it may or may not carry its own ND designation, not checked this pass.

name: The Fuchsmuhle Linden

location.address: Beside the Fuchsmuhle guesthouse on the Taubertalweg, Rothenburg ob der Tauber

verified_sources: https://www.lfu.bayern.de/gdi/wfs/natur/schutzgebiete?SERVICE=WFS&VERSION=2.0.0&REQUEST=GetFeature&typeNames=natur_wfsschutzgebiete:naturdenkmal_punktfoermig&srsName=EPSG:4326 (register id ND-04850, 'ND Nr. 45 Linde', Bayerisches Landesamt fuer Umwelt, CC BY 4.0)
access: Free; the tree stands roadside on the public Taubertalweg cycle and walking path beside the Fuchsmuhle guesthouse, not inside the guesthouse grounds proper (register location text: 'an der Fuchsmuhle', i.e. 'by', not 'im Hof' / 'in the courtyard' as the blocked Gut Burgstall entry is worded)
transport: About 2 km downstream along the Taubertalweg from Rothenburg's old town; a level 25-30 minute walk or a short ride on the cycle path
verify_notes: Register-level candidate ND Nr. 45 (Bavaria Naturdenkmal register, entry ND-04850), coordinates are tree-level (point_count 1). The Landkreis Ansbach Naturdenkmal Wikipedia list gives only the same designation with no age or girth (Bemerkung column empty), so it counts as one source with the register. Second, independent confirmation of continued existence: the separate de.wikipedia article on Fuchsmuehle itself (not the ND list) states in the present tense 'Im Ort steht eine Linde, die als Naturdenkmal ausgezeichnet ist' (a linden stands in the place, designated a natural monument), with no removal note. This is the same technique that caught the Detwang linden (ND Nr. 44, same list) as dead: that place-specific Wikipedia article explicitly records the Detwang tree's crown breaking off in a storm the night of 1-2 March 2020 and its removal, in the past tense ('stand bis 2020'). The Fuchsmuehle article carries no such note and uses present tense, which is the best currency evidence found this pass, but it is not a dated photo or recent observation, hence flagged. No age or girth found in any source; species is only ever given as 'Linde' (lime/linden), not narrowed to a species; leave both for the page to ask the reader. Fuchsmuehle is a working guesthouse (Pension Fuchsmuehle, Taubertalweg 103) directly on the Tauber cycle path.

name: The Langenmuhle Linden

location.address: Beside the Langenmuhle mill on the Taubertalweg, Rothenburg ob der Tauber

verified_sources: https://www.lfu.bayern.de/gdi/wfs/natur/schutzgebiete?SERVICE=WFS&VERSION=2.0.0&REQUEST=GetFeature&typeNames=natur_wfsschutzgebiete:naturdenkmal_punktfoermig&srsName=EPSG:4326 (register id ND-04851, 'ND Nr. 46 Linde', Bayerisches Landesamt fuer Umwelt, CC BY 4.0)
access: Free; register location text is 'an der Langenmuhle' (by the mill, roadside), the same wording pattern as the Fuchsmuhle entry and distinct from the blocked Gut Burgstall courtyard entry. The Langenmuhle itself is a private residence/farm (a 15th-century main building and an 1875 stone barn), but the tree is described as standing by the mill on the valley road rather than inside its grounds
transport: About 2.3 km downstream along the Taubertalweg from Rothenburg's old town, roughly a 30 minute level walk
verify_notes: Register-level candidate ND Nr. 46 (Bavaria Naturdenkmal register, entry ND-04851), tree-level coordinates. Same pattern as the Fuchsmuhle linden: the Landkreis Ansbach ND list gives no age or girth, so it is one source together with the register. Second source is the place's own de.wikipedia article, which states in the present tense 'Im Ort steht eine Linde, die als Naturdenkmal ausgezeichnet ist', with no removal note, the same currency check that caught the Detwang tree (ND Nr. 44) as dead. No dated photo or recent observation found this pass, hence flagged. No age, girth or narrower species found anywhere; leave for the page to ask the reader. Note the Langenmuhle itself is described in sources as a private residence/farm property (main house 15th c., barn 1875) forming the northern edge of the Altstadt ensemble; the register's own wording places the tree 'an der Langenmuhle' (by, not in the courtyard of), so it is treated as roadside rather than private grounds, but this boundary was not checked on the ground and a future pass should confirm the tree is visible from the public road before this ships with full confidence.

name: The Vorbachtal Spruces

location.address: In the Vorbach valley, about 300 m southeast of Durrenhof, near the hamlet of Vorbach, Rothenburg ob der Tauber

verified_sources: https://www.lfu.bayern.de/gdi/wfs/natur/schutzgebiete?SERVICE=WFS&VERSION=2.0.0&REQUEST=GetFeature&typeNames=natur_wfsschutzgebiete:naturdenkmal_punktfoermig&srsName=EPSG:4326 (register id ND-04852, 'ND Nr. 47 2 Fichten am Wasserfall im Vorbachtal', Bayerisches Landesamt fuer Umwelt, CC BY 4.0)
access: Free; the valley is reached by a public Gemeindeverbindungsstrasse (local connecting road) and is on the route of the W8 'Postbotenweg' waymarked hiking trail out of Rothenburg, which passes directly through the Vorbachtal and the neighbouring hamlet of Vorbach
transport: About 2.5 km west of Rothenburg's Marktplatz via the W8 Postbotenweg trail through the Vorbachtal; roughly 35-40 minutes on foot
verify_notes: Register-level candidate ND Nr. 47, a paired natural monument: two spruces (2 Fichten) at a small waterfall in the Vorbach valley, one collectible ensemble with one obvious spot to stand rather than a wood or avenue. Coordinates are tree-level in both the register and the Landkreis Ansbach Wikipedia ND list (identical to within rounding). Second, independent source: the de.wikipedia article on the hamlet of Vorbach itself states in the present tense 'Oestlich des Weilers stehen zwei Fichten, die als Naturdenkmal ausgezeichnet sind' (east of the hamlet stand two spruces designated a natural monument), no removal note, same currency-check technique used elsewhere in this pass. The municipal W8 Postbotenweg trail leaflet (Verkehrsverein Rothenburg ob der Tauber e.V., dated 2018) routes hikers directly through 'Vorbachtal' and past 'Duerrnhof' (its stops 4 and 6), confirming this is a real, signposted, walkable public route, though the leaflet does not name the spruces or the waterfall specifically. No age, girth or a dated photo of the waterfall or the spruces found this pass, hence flagged. 'Wasserfall' in the register name should be read as a small stream feature in a narrow wooded valley (the wider area has disused limestone quarries and is described as a scenic gorge), not a large or famous waterfall; the story should not oversell it.
